name: Chicago Police and Firefighter Training Academy (CPFTA)
org: Chicago Public Schools with Chicago Police, Fire and City Colleges
what_you_do: This two-year after-school program is for juniors and seniors. You apply as a sophomore. Classes meet twice a week at the Police or Fire Academy. Qualified students can earn OSHA, CPR and EMT-B certifications. It leads to a path into City Colleges.
grades: Apply in 10th grade; program runs 11th and 12th grade
who_can_apply: Sophomores who live in the city of Chicago. A 2.3 GPA and 90% attendance are recommended. Needs 2 letters of recommendation, evidence of a current physical exam and a background check.
pay_detail: Free: uniforms, materials, snacks and transportation help provided; scholarships possible. A paid summer internship between junior and senior year is possible (pay not stated).
duration: Two years; Tuesday and Wednesday 4:30 to 7:30 p.m., September to May
deadline_text: The application for the class of 2028 is closed. The class of 2029 application opens in December 2026 (no exact day posted). Info sessions run in winter and spring 2027.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the class of 2029 application opens. Provide 2 letters of recommendation, evidence of a current physical exam and pass a background check. Questions: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.
notes: Takes up to 125 students each year. The main page still says applications begin in February, but the application page says December 2026. Contact: cpfta@cps.edu or 773-553-2486.
